doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Staying home, image and being a woman leader
title: Recording for Perception Records and Johnny Pate
summary: While home she made Where Are You Going? for a Chicago label, Perception, dedicated to her daughter.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: During that period you were also recording for Steeplechase. Can you talk about that experience?
No, that wasn‘t Steeplechase then. That was . . . it was something called . . . see, I was home. I was doing Perception.
Oh yeah, Where Are You Going?
Yeah. I dedicated to my daughter. My daughter was like twelve, almost thirteen years old, right. And there was another one on another label. I didn‘t make any money, but you know, I was just . . .

No, in Chicago, Chicago. I met one guy that, Perception, we talk all the time. He‘s a sweet man. He wrote a lot of songs, a lot of great songs. He wrote [sings] ―Have you tried to forget? When your lover has left you, it‘s so hard to forget someone you loved.‖ He did two albums there. Johnny Pate, yeah.
Perception. But he came in here from Chicago. He knew John Levy and he came in, and I did . . . you remember [sings] ―Don‘t be on the outside looking on the inside‖?
Somebody asked me for that last week. We were in San Francisco. Okay.
